newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Drug baron charged for funding Colombian elections.
newsitem.headline: Drug baron charged for funding Colombian elections.

text.p: Colombia's chief prosecutor on Thursday charged a top drug trafficker with illegally funding 1994 presidential election campaigning, formally linking him to a scandal that has dogged President Ernesto Samper.

Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso ordered Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, the captured No.2 kingpin of the Cali drug cartel, to be held without bail. The fallen drug baron faces separate charges of drug trafficking and illicit enrichment.
Valdivieso's order did not specifically name which candidate's campaign had received the cocaine money.
But his office has been investigating allegations that the Cali cartel pumped more than $6 million into Samper's campaign coffers.

A congressional investigation cleared the president of any wrongdoing in June, but the allegations caused Colombia's worst political crisis in decades, prompting repeated calls for Samper's resignation.
Vice President Humberto de la Calle quit two weeks ago, saying Samper's alleged connections with drug barons had undermined the government's credibility.
The United States government revoked Samper's visa to travel to the United States in July, citing his ties to drug traffickers.

Rodriguez Orejuela has been held in Bogota's maximum security La Picota prison since he was captured by police last August. His brother Gilberto, the billionaire head of the Cali cartel was caught two months earlier.
